name: Sony PlayStation 2 family
summary: Explore PS2 fat and slim hardware and homebrew entry points: FreeMcBoot on memory card or hard drive for fat models, and FreeDVDBoot on all slims.

specs.memory: 32 MB RDRAM main memory + 4 MB embedded video memory
specs.storage: 8 MB memory card; hard drive in the fat models' expansion bay

variants.storage: Internal HDD via expansion bay (network adapter required)
variants.notes: SCPH-10000 through SCPH-55000 and SCPH-3000x/3500x/37000/390xx groups. Expansion bay for a hard drive and network adapter; early 10000-series use a PC-card-style expansion.

variants.storage: No internal HDD; 8 MB memory card
variants.notes: SCPH-700xx through 900xx groups. Internal power supply, no expansion bay; Ethernet built in.

firmware.version: N/A (BIOS fixed per model; no online updates)

homebrew.name: FreeMcBoot / FreeHDBoot (FMCB/FHDB)
homebrew.firmware: Every model; memory-card route works on all PS2; hard-drive route requires a fat model with network adapter and HDD
homebrew.summary: An installer that puts a boot loader on a memory card (FMCB) or on a hard drive (FHDB), so homebrew starts with the console. The installer is freely available from the community.

compatibility.note: Memory-card boot works on all PS2 models. The installer version current on psdevwiki is v1.9x, upgraded from the original v1.8C.
Hard-drive booting (FHDB) requires the network adapter and an installed HDD; slims have no expansion bay.

requirements: A memory card for FMCB; or a network adapter and IDE HDD for FHDB (fat models only).
warnings: Memory cards are old; failing cards can corrupt the FMCB install. Keep a spare card and a backup of the FMCB install.

homebrew.name: FreeDVDBoot
homebrew.firmware: Slim: all models supported; fat: version-specific (DVD Player versions 2.10, 2.12, 3.04; Sony patched the exploit in 2.14)
homebrew.summary: A DVD-player exploit that lets a burned DVD boot homebrew on an unmodified console. All PS2 Slim and Bravia TV units are supported per upstream; a phat needs the ISO matching its DVD Player version.

compatibility.note: Upstream states every PS2 Slim and Bravia TV unit is supported, with no per-version ISO needed.
Upstream lists DVD Player versions 2.10, 2.12 and 3.04 as supported on fat models, with a note that Sony patched the exploit in 2.14.

requirements: A DVD drive on the console and a computer with a disc burner.
Console language set to English (the exploit is language-dependent).
A DVD-R disc; rewritable media puts more strain on the laser.
warnings: Burn at the lowest speed and finalise the disc; failing to do so may cause read errors.
Console must be set to English language; other languages change memory contents and break the exploit.

homebrew.name: Open PS2 Loader (OPL)
homebrew.firmware: No firmware dependency: OPL is a PS2 application launched from an existing entry point such as FMCB/FHDB or FreeDVDBoot.
homebrew.summary: An open-source game and application loader for the PS2. It plays games from USB storage, MX4SIO SD adapters, iLink (IEEE 1394) devices, SMB shares, or an internal HDD/SSD in a fat console.

compatibility.note: Upstream describes OPL as a PS2 application loader; it depends on a homebrew entry point, not a system version.

requirements: A working PS2 entry point such as FMCB/FHDB or FreeDVDBoot.
A supported storage source: USB drive, MX4SIO adapter, iLink device, SMB share, or an internal drive in a fat console.
warnings: Game compatibility and load speed vary by storage type and title.
homebrew.availability: Open source (AFL-3.0); builds published by the project.

homebrew.name: wLaunchELF
homebrew.firmware: No firmware dependency: a PS2 application launched from an existing entry point.
homebrew.summary: An open-source file manager and executable launcher for the PS2, formerly known as uLaunchELF. It adds a text editor, hard-drive manager and FTP support.

compatibility.note: Upstream describes a PS2 application; it runs under any working homebrew entry point.

requirements: A PS2 entry point such as FMCB/FHDB or FreeDVDBoot.
warnings: File operations can delete data; back up memory cards and drives before moving system files.
homebrew.availability: Open source; releases published by the project.

homebrew.name: Kernelloader (PS2 Linux bootloader)
homebrew.firmware: No firmware dependency: a homebrew bootloader that starts a Linux kernel and initrd from memory card, USB, network share or the Live Linux DVD.
homebrew.summary: A free, open-source bootloader for PS2 Linux, the community replacement for Sony's discontinued commercial Linux kit. The project also ships a BlackRhino-based Live Linux DVD that boots on fat and slim consoles without a modchip.

compatibility.note: The project's hardware table lists fat models from V1 through V11 as working; its site states Linux runs stably on the fat PS2.
The project's hardware table lists slim V12/V13 and V14+ as working with network support, but calls USB write access unstable and recommends the Live Linux DVD.

requirements: A homebrew entry point such as FMCB, a memory card exploit or Action Replay Media Player.
A Linux kernel (vmlinux) and initrd on memory card, USB or a network share; or the Live Linux DVD.
For a hard-drive install, a fat console with network adapter and HDD.
warnings: Slim PSTwo support is less stable: the project notes unstable USB write access and recommends the Live DVD or an SMB share.
Sony's official PS2 Linux kit is discontinued and does not support slim consoles.
The Live DVD is a video DVD: the console reads burned video DVDs without a modchip, but a homebrew loader must be started before the disc is inserted.
homebrew.availability: Open source (GPLv2/AFL); releases and the Live Linux DVD published on SourceForge.
